ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two cascaded JK flip-flops. The left input clock CP is connected to the clock terminal C of the first-stage flip-flop; the output Q of the first stage is connected to the clock terminal C of the second-stage flip-flop; the right-side output terminal of the second stage is labeled Q2. In the figure, logic “1” is connected to the J and K inputs of the flip-flops, making each stage of the JK flip-flop work in the toggle state of J=K=1. Reasoning: When J=K=1 of a JK flip-flop, for each arriving effective clock edge, the output toggles once, so each stage divides the input pulse frequency by 2. The frequency of the first-stage output Q1 is f_CP/2; it serves as the clock input of the second stage, so the frequency of the second-stage output Q2 is (f_CP/2)/2 = f_CP/4. It is known that the frequency of Q2 is f2, therefore f2 = f_CP/4, obtaining f_CP = 4 f2.

method.method_draft: Treat the two flip-flops as a 2-bit binary ripple counter. Starting from any stable state, each CP pulse toggles the first bit Q1; the second bit Q2 toggles only when the first stage supplies the appropriate clock edge.
